evidence: The survivor orders vertices by degree for "better pruning" and uses a three-valued colors array; the statement says versions "must share exactly one active channel" and that equal versions "share two active channels."
affordance_in_statement: Version 1 activates channels X and Y; Version 2 activates channels Y and Z; Version 3 activates channels Z and X. For each link, the protocol versions ... must share exactly one active channel. If they share two active channels, ... the link fails.
removal_suggestion: Do not state the three channel pairs and the equality/interference consequence together. Present compatibility indirectly, for example through a neutral compatibility table or a scenario-specific interaction rule, so that the solver must derive the constraint instead of immediately recognizing that every edge simply requires different values. This preserves the same constraints while removing the conspicuous coloring cue.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Recognizes the instance as three-coloring and searches assignments with bitmask adjacency, degree ordering, and pruning.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: Each edge permits exactly pairs of distinct protocol versions, since any two different channel pairs share one channel while equal pairs share two.

common_affordance: The channel rules collapse every communication-link constraint to the requirement that its endpoints receive different values from {1,2,3}, i.e. ordinary graph 3-coloring.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Uses straightforward sequential backtracking over all three versions with only local equality checks and no effective variable ordering or stronger pruning, causing exponential search and TLE on difficult instances.
Likewise relies on naive recursive coloring/backtracking rather than a robust exact-coloring search strategy, so hard 3-coloring instances exhaust the search space.

recommended_edit: Replace the explicit channel-pair bullets and direct interference explanation with an indirect compatibility specification embedded in the network scenario, requiring the solver to derive which version pairs are allowed while keeping the same three versions, links, input, output, bounds, and examples.
regression_risk: This may make the already-defeated naive solvers appear conceptually less likely to recognize the problem, but it will not repair their exponential search; the main risk is that a stronger model reconstructs the same coloring reduction from the indirect rule.
